 Rolls-Royce and Skanska Roll Out Earthquake-Resistant SMRs 
 Rolls-Royce SMR is getting a major safety upgrade with an earthquake-resistant component capable of being built off-site. 
 Save 
 Saved 
 Listen to Article 
 Rolls-Royce SMR and Skanska hit a major milestone in nuclear power plants powered by small modular reactors ( SMRs ). Skanska built and tested a first-of-its-kind aseismic bearing (earthquake-resistant) pedestal demonstrator at Cementation Skanska’s Bentley Works facility in Doncaster, South Yorkshire, England.
 The demonstrator will play a vital role in the Rolls-Royce SMR design, as it will support structural isolation devices. During seismic events, those devices help separate buildings and infrastructure from ground movement, which helps keep the power plant safer and more resilient. One of the biggest accomplishments is that the teams proved they can build this critical component off-site.
 Testing Before Building 
 A prototype aseismic bearing pedestal demonstrator for Rolls-Royce SMR; Photo: Skanska 
 The demonstrator is part of Rolls-Royce SMR’s plan to test and prove construction methods before using them on future power plants. Producing parts away from the final building site can give teams better control over production, quality, and scheduling. Additionally, it helps make construction more predictable.
 Advertisement
 “The successful completion of this demonstrator marks an important step in developing a factory-built approach to delivering our SMRs,” said Ruth Todd, Operations and Supply Chain Director, Rolls-Royce SMR. “Our delivery program is ramping up. By testing and refining critical components ahead of deployment, we can reduce risk, improve predictability and strengthen confidence in our fleet delivery model. The project also highlights the value of early collaboration with our supply chain partners, bringing together expertise from across manufacturing, engineering and construction as we industrialize the delivery of nuclear power plants.”
 Teamwork in the Factory 
 To pull this off, the program combined Skanska’s civil engineering and design skills with manufacturing and technical trials in Doncaster.
 “Successfully completing this demonstrator is an important achievement for both teams. It shows the value of collaboration in testing and proving the construction approach before moving into delivery,” Terry Muckian, Executive Vice President, Skanska UK, said . “By combining our civil engineering, design, steelwork manufacturing and off-site construction expertise, we have demonstrated how this critical component can be produced in a controlled factory environment. We are proud to be working with Rolls-Royce SMR and to be able to bring Skanska’s experience and expertise to the next generation of nuclear energy.”
